FOREWORD This Indian Standard was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards on 3 April 1989, after the draft finalized by the Power Capacitors Sectional Committee had been approved by the Electrotechnical Division Council. It is intended to formulate uniform requirements regarding performance and testing of internal fuses for series capacitors. This standard also provides a guide for coordination of fuse protection to series capacitors covered in IS 9835 : 1981 `Specification for series capacitors for power systems'. The fuses conforming to this standard are designed to isolate faulted capacitor elements to allow the operation of remaining parts of that capacitor unit and the bank in which the capacitor unit is connected. Such fuses are not a substitute for a switching device such as a circuit breaker, or the external protection of the capacitor bank, or part thereof. The design of internal fuse is specifically matched with that of the series capacitor. This standard is based on the following publications/documents cal Commission (IEC): issued by the International Electrotechni-

a) IEC Pub 595 (1977) and Amendment No. 1 (April 1980) Internal fuses for series capacitors; and b) Dot : 33(C.O)72 Draft Amendment No. 2 to IEC Pub 595 (1977).

1 SCOPE 1.1 This standard covers the requirements, tests and guidance for coordination of fuses used to protect series capacitors in accordance with 1s 9835 : 1981 `Specification for series capacitors for power systems'. 3.4 Unbalance Protection

A device sensitive to capacitance difference between branches of the bank normally in balance with each other. The capacitance difference may be due to a blown fuse(s), or insulation failure within the bank.
NOTE - Other protective devices, such as, overcurrent and earth fault protection, are self-explanatory since they are commonly used for other application.

1.2 This standard does not apply to fuses for which the service conditions, in general, are incompatible with the requirements of the standard unless otherwise agreed between the manufacturer and the purchaser. 1.3 The guidance for coordination is given in Annex A. 2 REFERENCES 2.1 The, following Indian adjuncts to this standard: IS NO. IS 12677:1989 6 WITHSTAND REQUIREMENTS 6.1 After operations, the fuse assembly must withstand full element voltage plus any unbalance voltage due to fuse action and any short-time transient overvoltage normally experienced during the life of the capacitor. 6.2 Throughout the life of the capacitor, the fuse shall be capable of continuously carrying a current equal to or greater than the maximum permissible unit current ( see 5.1 of IS 9835 : 1981) divided by the number of parallel fused paths. 6.3 The fuse connected to the undamaged element(s) must be able to carry the discharge currents due to the breakdown of element(s). 6.4 The fuses must be able to carry the currents due to short-circuit faults external to the unit(s) on the occurring within the voltage range in accordance with 5. 7 MARKING 7.1 The marking regarding the presence of internal fuse in capacitor shall be provided on the rating plate of the series capacitor. 8 TESTS 8.1 Type Tests The following shall constitute type tests: a) Discharge test (9 ), and b) Disconnecting test ( 10 ). 9 DISCHARGE TEST 9.1 The fuses shall be subjected test stated in IS 9835 : 1981.

9.2 To prove that the fuses have not operated, capacitance measurement shall be made before and after the test. A measuring method shall be used that is sufficiently sensitive to detect the capacitance change caused by one blown fuse.

ANNEX

A

( Clause 1.3 )
GUIDE FOR CO-ORDINATION A-l GENERAL A-l.1 The fuse is connected in series with the element that the fuse is designed to isolate if the element becomes faulty. After the breakdown of an element, the fuse connected to it will blow and isolate it from the remaining part of the capacitor, which allows the unit to continue in service. A-l.2 The blowing of one or more fuses will cause voltage changes within the bank. A-l.3 The voltage across sound unit(s) must not exceed the value given in the relevant standard. A-l.4 Depending upon the internal connection of the units, the blowing of one or more fuses may also cause a change of voltage within the unit. A-l.5 The remaining elements in a series group will have an increased working voltage and the manufacturer shall, on request, give details of the voltage rise caused by the blown fuses. OF FUSE PROTECTION

The number of breakdowns at each voltage limit shall, in such cases, be subject to agreement between the manufacturer and the purchaser. If the number of breakdowns is exceeded, the vo!tages stated in 10.4 may have to be increased. 4 To verify the current limiting behaviour of the fuses when tested at the upper voltage limit, the voltage drop, excluding transient, across the blown fuse must not exceed 30 percent.

B-2 CAPACITOR

PREHEATING

B-2.1 The capacitor unit is preheated in a chamber before applying the ac test voltage at the lower limit. Preheating temperature ( 100 to 150�C) is chosen by the manufacturer to achieve a practical short time (from few minutes to few hours) to the first breakdown. B-2.2 A lower preheating temperature should be used when applying the test voltage at the higher voltage limit, to avoid breakdowns before reaching the test voltage. B-2.3 Capacitor the test. current is to be recorded during

B-5 ELECTRICAL BREAKDOWN OF THE ELEMENT ( SECOND SOLUTION ) B-5.1 Some elements in the test unit are each provided with, for example, a short fuse connected to two extra tabs and inserted between the dielectric layers. Each tab is connected to its own bushing. B-5.2 The test voltage may be dc or ac, the choice being left to the manufacturer. B-5.3 To with this sufficient connected obtain breakdown of an element equipped short fuse wire, a capacitor charged at a voltage is connected to the two bushings to it in order to explode the wire.

B-3.2 If ac voltage is used, capacitor current is to be recorded during the test and timing of puncture is to be made, to ascertain that the breakdown is triggered to take place at the instant of the peak of the ac test voltage, or very near to it.
NOTES 1 Puncture

of only one element cannot be guaranteed.

2 In order to limit the possibility of a flashover to the container along the nail, or through the hole caused by the nail, the punctures may be performed to the elements connected, permanently or during the test, to the container. 3 dc voltage is especially all elements in parallel. suitable for capacitors having

B-5.4 In the case of ac voltage, the connection of the charged capacitor causing the wire explosion must be triggered at the instant of the peak voltage or very near to it. F;$:esZapacitor current is to be recorded during

B-4 ELECTRICAL BREAKDOWN OF THE ELEMENT ( FIRST SOLUTION ) B-4.1 Some elements in the test unit are each provided with, for example, a tab, inserted between the dielectric layers. Each tab is connected to a separate terminal. B-4.2 The test voltage may be ac or dc, the choice being left to the manufacturer. B-4.3 To obtain breakdown of an element thus equipped, a surge voltage of sufficient amplitude is applied between the tab and one of the foils of the modified element. B-4.4 In the case of ac voltage, the surge must be triggered at the instant of the peak or very near to it.

B-6 ELECTRICAL BREAKDOWN OF THE ELEMENT ( THIRD SOLUTION ) B-6.1 A small part of an element ( or some elements ) in a unit is at the time of manufacture removed and replaced with a weaker dielectric. For example, lo-20 cm2 of a film - paper - film dielectric is punched away and the hole is covered with two thin papers. B-6.2 This method will require experience on how to make a suitable dielectric strength reduction.

Standard marked products are also continuously checked by BIS for conformity to that standard as a further safeguard.
